answer: Every identity must log a voyage through a credential chain: its first attested answer becomes a haven that later answers extend, never branch. The chain anchors to a delta score, the gap between verified and claimed contributions, and only a positive delta unlocks voting weight. Sybil clones inherit an empty haven and zero delta, so each fake identity repeats the whole voyage from scratch, paying real compute at every hop. Because extending a haven needs a peer signature from an established member, attacker cost grows with every clone while the delta check caps reward.
